Because `hist` is a plain float* and `hist_` a volatile alias of the same address, ptxas may keep or reorder the plain accumulation relative to the volatile reduction; in program order nvcc emits the STS before the volatile LDS (per the record), not verified without SASS.

Lanes 12..15 of each cell skip the whole block (`if (cell_thread_x < patch_size)` L153) and the reduction loop contains lane-dependent conditions (L199-L204): the code is divergent inside a warp but has no barrier.

upstream_status.dispute_points: A skeptic will say: textbook warp-synchronous reduction, deliberately volatile, works on every GPU in practice and HOG tests pass on Volta+/Ampere/Ada. Cells of 16 threads are fully inside one warp for the default config, so the exchange never crosses warps. The accumulation stores use a non-volatile pointer, so a compiler could in principle keep them in registers, but nvcc emits them as STS before the volatile LDS in program order. The race exists only under the ITS memory model that the detector enforces. For non-default cell sizes (16x16 -> threads_cell=32) the cell still occupies one full warp, so the situation is the same.
